deep.title: Gemini 4 Argon: our next era of frontier intelligence
deep.score_reason: Gemini 4 Argon是Google新一代旗舰正式发布，确立新范式，直接影响模型选型。
deep.analysis:
这是 Google DeepMind 发布的下一代前沿模型 Gemini 4 Argon 的官方公告，标志着 Gemini 系列进入了一个新的能力阶段。

此前，大模型在复杂推理、长上下文理解和多模态融合上存在明显短板。具体表现为：面对需要多步逻辑推导的数学或编程问题，模型容易在中间步骤出错；处理超长文档时，关键信息会随着上下文增长而被“遗忘”；视觉与语言信息的结合也常常停留在表面描述，难以进行深层因果推理。这些痛点限制了 AI 从“演示级”走向“生产级”的跨越。

Gemini 4 Argon 的核心突破在于系统级的架构革新。它采用了原生多模态训练范式，不是先分开训练文本和图像模块再拼接，而是从一开始就让模型在交织的文本、图像、音频数据中学习，这使得视觉推理不再是对图片的“看图说话”，而是能理解图表中的趋势、照片中的物理因果关系。在推理层面，模型引入了更高效的测试时计算扩展机制——通俗讲，就是模型在回答复杂问题时，内部会动态分配更多“思考时间”和计算资源，自动进行多路径探索与验证，从而在数学证明、代码生成等任务上显著降低了中间步骤的幻觉率。此外，其上下文窗口实现了质的扩展，并配合改进的注意力机制，确保在百万级 token 的长上下文中，对开头和中间部分信息的召回准确率不会衰减，这让它真正具备了处理整本小说、完整代码库或全年财报的能力。

对 AI 应用岗而言，这条资讯的面试价值在于“生产可用性”的论证。面试官可能会问“如何评估一个新模型是否值得接入业务”，你可以引用 Gemini 4 Argon 的改进点来构建回答框架：一看推理可控性，即模型能否在复杂业务流程中保持逻辑一致，这对应其测试时计算扩展；二看多模态融合深度，即能否处理业务中混合的图文数据，这对应其原生多模态训练；三看长程记忆稳定性，即处理长文档或长对话时状态是否一致，这对应其长上下文注意力优化。更重要的是，你可以主动抛出观点：下一代 AI 应用的核心壁垒不再是“调用模型 API”，而是如何围绕这类具备深度推理和多模态理解能力的模型，设计出能利用其“动态思考”特性的产品交互与任务拆解流程。

deep.title: How to Build a Model Router in the Harness
deep.summary: How we built a model router into Open SWE's harness that cut median cost per coding task by 64% with no measurable drop in quality, and how to build your own.
deep.score_reason: Open SWE 官方博客，模型路由方法可复现，成本降低64%且质量无损，直接解决生产中的成本与质量平衡问题
deep.analysis:
在 Open SWE（一个开源软件工程智能体项目）的评估框架中，团队构建了一个模型路由器，能在不降低任务完成质量的前提下，将每个编码任务的中位成本降低 64%。简单说，这是一个根据任务难度自动选择不同模型的调度层，让简单任务用便宜模型、复杂任务才调用昂贵模型。

此前，这类 SWE-Bench 风格评测的痛点在于成本与性能的权衡。如果全用顶尖模型（如 Claude Opus），成本极高；全用廉价模型，复杂任务又做不好。更麻烦的是，任务难度无法提前标注——同一个代码库修复问题，有的只需改一行配置，有的要跨多个文件重构逻辑。传统做法要么一刀切，要么靠人工经验判断，缺乏系统性的自动化方案。

该路由器的技术流程分三步。第一步是训练一个“难度分类器”，它不直接预测任务能否完成，而是判断任务属于“简单”还是“困难”。训练数据来自历史评测记录：将每个任务用强模型和弱模型分别求解，如果弱模型也能解决，就标为简单；只有强模型能解决的标为困难。分类器的输入是任务描述文本，输出是二分类标签。第二步是部署阶段的路由决策：新任务先过分类器，若判为简单则发给弱模型（成本低），判为困难则发给强模型（能力强）。第三步是成本与质量监控：在评测集上对比纯强模型、纯弱模型和路由策略的表现，确认中位成本下降 64% 的同时，任务解决率没有可测量的下降。整个路由器集成在 Open SWE 的 Harness（评测执行框架）中，作为模型调用的前置中间层。

对 AI 应用岗而言，这个案例有多个可谈点。首先是“成本-质量”的工程权衡，面试中常被问到如何降低大模型调用成本，这个路由器提供了一个数据驱动的自动化方案，而非简单的缓存或 prompt 压缩。其次是分类器的设计思路：用强弱模型的能力差作为自动标注信号，避免了昂贵的人工标注，这体现了“用模型能力差异生成训练数据”的实用技巧。第三是生产可用的架构模式——路由器作为无侵入的中间层，不改动下游 Agent 逻辑，易于集成和回退。面试时可以延伸讨论：如果业务场景没有现成的强弱模型对比数据，如何冷启动？分类器误判的代价如何度量？这些都能展示你在 AI 应用落地上的系统思考。

However, existing methods primarily optimize how the harness is updated while largely fixing which training scenarios generate the feedback that drives those updates. As the harness evolves, the scenarios most useful for further optimization can change, suggesting that the training curriculum itself should adapt alongside the harness. We formulate this missing dimension of harness optimization as an automated curriculum learning problem and introduce ActiveSaddler. It abstracts recurring failures into reusable failure-pattern arms, estimates the potential learning progress from further targeting each pattern, and adaptively balances revisiting known weaknesses with exploring unseen scenarios for new ones. deep.analysis:
这是一篇关于如何让 AI Agent 的“装备”自动进化的研究，核心思想是：不仅优化 Agent 的提示词和工具，还要同步优化用来训练它的“考题”顺序。

它解决的是当前 Agent 优化方法中的一个盲点。现有工作在迭代更新 Agent 的提示词、工具接口和控制逻辑时，往往使用一套固定的训练场景来产生反馈。这就像让一个学生反复刷同一套卷子，即使他的能力在变化，考题的难度和类型却一成不变。随着 Agent 的“装备”不断进化，能带来最大提升的场景也在动态变化，固定顺序的训练场景会逐渐失效，无法持续提供有价值的反馈。

ActiveSaddler 的技术核心是将训练场景的编排建模为一个“非平稳老虎机”问题，并让课程与装备协同进化。通俗讲，“老虎机”是一种在探索与利用间做决策的算法框架，而“非平稳”意味着奖励概率会随时间变化，这正好对应了装备进化后，不同训练场景的价值会动态改变这一特性。具体流程上，它首先从执行反馈中抽象出反复出现的失败模式，将其作为老虎机的“臂”。然后，它估算针对每种失败模式继续训练可能带来的学习收益，并自适应地平衡两种行为：一是重温已知的弱点，二是探索未见过的场景以发现新的失败模式。最关键的是，优化结果会持续更新已发现的失败模式集合及其优先级，使得训练课程能与装备同步演化。实验在 GAIA2 和 Terminal-Bench 2.0 上验证了效果，相比使用固定场景顺序的优化器，Pass@1 指标分别提升了 4.4 和 7.5 个百分点，消融实验也证实了这些收益确实依赖于动态构建课程。

对 AI 应用岗而言，这条资讯提供了两个可直接在面试中引用的工程视角。第一，它揭示了 Agent 生产落地时的一个关键瓶颈：静态评测集无法驱动持续优化。你可以借此阐述，构建一个能根据 Agent 表现自适应调整的“训练场”或“回归测试集”，是提升系统长期可靠性的核心手段。第二，它展示了如何将一个抽象的算法问题（非平稳老虎机）转化为具体的工程模块（失败模式抽象、优先级动态更新），这体现了将学术方法落地为可运行系统的能力。在面试中讨论 Agent 架构设计或优化流程时，主动提出“训练数据的课程学习应该与模型/装备同步迭代”这一观点，并结合探索与利用的平衡策略，会是一个很有深度的加分项。

mid.title: RPTune: Learned Context Curation for LLM Catalog Search
mid.summary: For small merchant businesses (SMBs) whose catalogs fit within a long-context LLM, full-catalog prompting offers a compelling alternative to multi-stage retrieval designed primarily for large marketplaces with millions of items. However, fitting the full catalog into the context window does not ensure that the model can use it effectively, since LLMs do not exploit long contexts uniformly. We therefore study in-context catalog search through two complementary questions: (1) how to curate and present catalogs to the LLM, and (2) how to adapt the LLM for product selection on curated contexts. We propose RPTune, an end-to-end framework that couples learned catalog curation with LLM post-training using automatically generated, catalog-grounded supervision. An encoder-reorganizer curator orders and prunes products guided by downstream LLM feedback, while the resulting curated catalogs in turn improve the effectiveness of LLM post-training with a context-relative reward. We evaluate RPTune on 7 real merchants spanning distinct retail verticals, using 100 complex conversational queries per merchant. RPTune consistently improves search accuracy across both proprietary and open-weight LLMs, with context curation yielding gains of up to 31.4 percentage points and post-training adding a further 10.3 points on average.

paper.title: Beyond Memory: Harnessing Long-Horizon Agents with Explicit Belief States
paper.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents can now undertake increasingly complex tasks, but the way they organize interaction history into memory does not ensure a coherent understanding of the current world. We introduce PoS, an inference-time framework that constructs and continually maintains explicit belief states as the agent's decision context. Each belief combines an estimate of the current world state with unresolved task requirements, making explicit what the agent still needs to learn and accomplish. To keep this belief reliable and actionable, PoS validates its consistency and monitors task progress to detect Belief Trapping, where the agent continues to act without making meaningful progress toward the goal. Recovery is then tailored to both the trapping pattern and the type of unresolved task requirement. Experiments on four benchmarks spanning execution and diagnosis show that PoS achieves the highest overall performance on every benchmark with all three LLM backbones. Ablations demonstrate the importance of consistency validation and recovery, while context-scaling experiments show resilience to context growth. Together, these results support belief construction and continual maintenance as a foundation for long-horizon context management beyond history retention and compression.

paper.title: When Users Change Their Minds: Measuring and Repairing Intent Drift in LLM Agents
paper.summary: LLM agents often operate over multi-turn interactions in which user intent changes before execution. We study intent drift: the failure mode in which superseded parts of the user's intent continue to influence the final answer or tool action. We introduce IntentFlux, an executable benchmark that converts verifiable tasks into dialogues with controlled intent changes while preserving their original graders. In a 627-case calibration, mean task score falls from 0.476 to 0.384 as dialogues contain more superseded and withdrawn information. Across eight models, the rate of fully correct solutions is significantly lower when the same final task must be recovered from an evolving dialogue rather than given directly in a single turn. We further introduce StateForge, which explicitly maintains the active requirements before generation. On General-Test, it improves mean task score from 0.367 to 0.467. Providing the ground-truth final state improves performance further but still does not recover single-turn performance, indicating that state-estimation errors explain only part of the gap. These results establish intent drift as a measurable multi-turn failure mode and explicit state maintenance as a partial mitigation.

paper.title: Mem++: Non-Destructive Memory for Long-Term Organizational LLM Agents
paper.summary: Large Language Model (LLM) agents now take part in organizational work, where many authors record decisions across documents over months. Because a revised decision arrives as a new document rather than an edit, answering a question requires knowing which version held at a given time. However, most memory systems compress the record at write time. By distilling each document into facts, notes or graph edges, these methods fix what can be answered before any question is asked. To address this, we propose Mem++, a non-destructive memory framework shifting from write-time distillation to read-time selection. Mem++ stores every document whole with its date and author, and it calls no generative model at write time. At read time, it retrieves only documents dated up to the time a question asks about and fuses lexical and semantic rankings. Unlike systems that overwrite older versions, Mem++ keeps them and leaves the choice to the answering model. Evaluations on the organizational benchmark OrgMemBench demonstrate that Mem++ surpasses the strongest memory system baseline by 8.0 to 13.1 points across two answering models. With gpt-4.1-mini, it also achieves the best overall score, 2.6 points above RAG.
